terra.problem: Papa's claim about being passed from desk to desk invents an experience outside his established backstory.
Herod is mentioned without saying who he is.
Saying Pilate shows up later gives away what happens later in the story group.
The text says the other disciple brings Peter in, not that someone had to come and get him.
Papa refers to himself in the third person instead of speaking as I.
The comparison between making a fire and turning off a mixer is flat and doesn't land as a joke.
The passage gives Jesus' answer next, but doesn't say how quickly He answered.
The claim about miracles in the Gospels goes beyond this passage and needs a reference.
The text doesn't say the listeners sat or that the soldiers tied knots.
Jesus points to those who heard His message. The explanation narrows them to people at the synagogues and temple, then assumes anyone present could tell what He said.
The passage doesn't describe Jesus' volume or say He answered calmly.
Papa claims to know what the baker wants, and saying the text doesn't give Peter a good ending yet suggests what happens later.
The passage doesn't say whether Peter expected to hear the rooster.
The passage doesn't establish that the fire is still burning or that it is early morning.
